title: Towards the construction of a virtual yeast.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and fully text-extracted the published PDF (12 pages, 97,434 characters) from the University of Luxembourg repository copy of the article. Searched the whole text: zero occurrences of 'Data availability', 'Code availability', 'Extended Data', 'Supplementary' or 'deposit'; the only web links are 15 reference DOIs and arXiv preprint links plus nature.com/reprints. Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N and no PMCID, so no supplementary file list exists to fetch. Crossref gives type=journal-article, Nature vol 655 pp 59-70, 67 authors, 150 references; the PDF header line reads 'Perspective'. Also opened the consortium's own project page (guomics.com/way), which lists five related publications and no downloads, no accessions and no code repository.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The description of the eight proposed function-centred modules, the three 'data pillars' (mechanistic knowledge, subcellular architecture, dynamic states) and the closed-loop active-learning design. All of this is a proposal for future work; none of it corresponds to files that exist today.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. There is no dataset. This is a Nature Perspective (a forward-looking roadmap article), not a research or resource paper. Full-text search of the published PDF found no data availability statement, no code availability statement, no supplementary files, no repository accession of any kind, and no GitHub or Zenodo link. Europe PMC confirms hasData=N and hasSuppl=N. Nothing to download, so the evaluation stops here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable: no table exists, so no column exists. The article proposes labels that would have to be generated by future experiments.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero rows are available. n_rows left null because nothing was counted.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: the paper reports no dataset counts to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable, but worth flagging: the article's vision is explicitly built on outputs of other AI models (a large-language-model orchestration layer calling domain models), so any 'labels' it would eventually emit would be model predictions, the exact circularity A8 warns about.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the article contains no data, so no model could be trained or evaluated from it.

plain_idea.one_liner: No project is possible here; the article is a plan for a future simulated yeast cell, with no data attached.
plain_idea.train_on: Nothing. The article describes data types it would like to have (mechanistic knowledge, subcellular architecture, dynamic cell states) but releases none; verified example count is zero.
plain_idea.predict: Nothing measurable. The proposed system would output simulated cell behaviour, but no ground-truth measurements accompany the article against which such output could be scored.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: The reference list is a useful map of which yeast resources the authors consider best (whole-genome knockout fitness screens, genetic-interaction maps, perturbation proteomics), so it is worth mining as a pointer to real candidate datasets published elsewhere.

ml_idea: None from this article. The only salvageable use is bibliographic: follow its 150 references to the primary yeast resources it builds on (for example Costanzo and Boone's genetic-interaction maps, yeast deletion-collection fitness screens, and the perturbation-proteomics foundation-model preprint it cites) and evaluate those primary papers as candidates instead.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no data to process.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search the published PDF for a data availability statement. It has none, and Europe PMC flags hasData=N and hasSuppl=N. Under five minutes, and it kills the candidate outright.

verdict_reason: A1 fails outright. This is a Nature Perspective piece (a 67-author roadmap for a future AI-driven yeast cell simulator), not a research or resource paper. Full text extraction of the published PDF shows no data availability statement, no code availability statement, no supplementary files and no repository accessions, and Europe PMC independently reports hasData=N and hasSuppl=N. There is literally nothing to download, count or model. Its value to this project is only as a bibliography pointing at the real yeast datasets it cites.
